 Judgment

The minor petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V.Act for seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by her in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief contents of the petition are as under:
SCCH - 09 3 MVC No.4324/2022 On 14.07.2022 at about 9.45 am., when the petitioner was walking on the foot path road near Government Hospital, Kabbali to Akknahalli cross road, Nugehalli Hobli,
Channarayapattna taluk Hassan District carefully observing traffic rules and regulations, on the left of the road, at that time, one motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-54-K-6198 came from back side in a rash and negligent manner without observing any of the traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner sustained right leg both bone fracture and other injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to near Gross Life Hospital at Channarayapattna wherein she took treatment as inpatient for 15 days and underwent CRIF and TENS implant was fixed.
Petitioner has spent Rs.2 lakhs towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
Prior to the accident, she was aged about 9 years and SCCH - 09 4 MVC No.4324/2022 she was hale and healthy and was student.
After the alleged accident she lost her education.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of riding of motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-54-K-6198 and the Neggehalli police has been registered a case under Crime No.102/2022 under Section 279, 337, 338 of IPC against the rider of said motor cycle.
The 1 st respondent being RC owner and 2nd respondent being insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
With all these contentions, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- under all head together with interest and costs.
3. In pursuance of the court notice, the respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their respective counsel and filed their respective objection statement.

4. The brief contents of objection statement of respondent No.1 are as under:-

sentences.text: The respondent No.1 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of averments made petition in toto.
Further the respondent No.1 is admitted that, he is the owner of the said motor cycle and the same is insured with the respondent No.2.
Further the respondent No.1 repeated the contents of the petition.

He has contended that, the accident was not occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle, on the other hand, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
The claim amount claimed by the petitioner without any basis and the same is exorbitant and the petitioner is not entitled the same.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the petition as against him.

5. The brief contents of objection statement of respondent No.2 are as under:-
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petition filed SCCH - 09 6 MVC No.4324/2022 by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
It has denied all the allegations made out in the claim petition.
The respondent No.2 has denied that the vehicle bearing No.KA-54-K-6198 was insured with this respondent and the insurance was not in force at the time of alleged accident.
The respondent denied the name, age, occupation of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant.

Further contended that, if at all the alleged accident has taken place it is only due to the negligence of the petitioner who was moving on the road negligently and dashed against the vehicle and false complaint was given against the rider of the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1.
The delay in lodging the complaint itself indicates the above aspect.
Further contended that, the rider of the motor cycle has no valid driving licence and said vehicle had no valid F.C. as on the date of accident.
Further the respondent No.2 contended that, the owner of the vehicle has not complied the mandatory provision as required U/Sec.134(c) of Motor SCCH - 09 7 MVC No.4324/2022 vehicles Act.

sentences.text: Further contended that, at the time of accident the driver of the bus was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle.
This respondent has right to contest the petition on behalf of owner of the vehicle also as per Sec.170 of M.V. Act.

Further contended that, the accident was not occurred due to negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the petition as against him.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the Tribunal has framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 14.07.2022 at about 9.45 a.m., the petitioner was pedestrian on the footpath near Government Hospital Kabbali to Akknahalli Cross road, Nugehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna Taluk, Hassan District, at that time,
the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-K-6198 came from back side SCCH - 09 8 MVC No.4324/2022 with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and Vinutha R vs Manzoor Ilahi on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58048457/
3 dashed against the petitioner.

Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries in the alleged RTA?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What Order or Award?

7. In order to prove the case, the guardian of the petitioner i.e., father has examined himself as PW.1 and petitioner has got examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW.2 and in all got marked the documents as Ex-P-1 to Ex.P.28.
On the other hand, the respondent did not choose to adduce the evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the records.

The petitioner has filed following citations:
1. AIR 1980 Sc 1354 2. ILR 2003 KAR 493 3. 2007 (4) KCCR 2810 4. (2011)4 SCC 693 5. (2014) 14 SCC 396.

Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1: It is the case of the petitioner that, on 14.07.2022 at about 9.45 am.,
when she was walking on the foot path road near Government Hospital, Kabbali to Akknahalli cross road, Nugehalli Hobli, Channarayapattna taluk Hassan District carefully observing traffic rules and regulations, on the left of the road, at that time,

In order to substantiate the same, the father of petitioner got examined as PW-1 and produced the documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex-P26.

The petitioner SCCH - 09 10 MVC No.4324/2022 produced the FIR as per Ex.P.1, complaint as per Ex.P.2, crime details attest mahazar as per Ex.P.3, sketch as per Ex.P.4, seizer mahazar as per Ex.P.5, vehicle release mahazar as per Ex.P.6, IMV report as per Ex.P.11 and charge sheet as per Ex.P.12.

On perusal of those documents, after the accident, the complaint has been lodged by the father of petitioner before the Nuggehalli Police Station against the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-K-6198.

Spot panchanama has been prepared as per Ex.P.4 and after investigation the I.O has filed charge sheet against the rider of the offending motor cycle for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of I.P.C, the charge sheet is produced as per Ex.P.12.

The MVA report is produced as per Ex.P.11.
12.

On perusal of these documents, it discloses that, on 14.07.2022 the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-54-K-6198 ridden the same in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as a result, petitioner sustained grievous SCCH - 09 11 MVC No.4324/2022 injury.

The petitioner has also produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.10 which discloses right tibia shaft fracture, right fibula shaft fracture and abrasion over closure of right foot injuries sustained by the petitioner and doctor opined injury No.1 and 2 are grievous and injury No.3 is simple in nature.
Though the respondent No.2 has cross-examined the PW1 and suggested to the PW-1 that, due to the negligence of the petitioner accident was occurred, but said suggestion has been denied by the PW-1.
Further respondent No.2 argued that, the accident occurred on 14.07.2022 but the complaint has been lodged on 16.07.2022 there was 2 days delay in lodging the complaint.

As per Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 911 (Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayan and others), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - "lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting claim application".
In that reported case, injured was the minor boy SCCH - 09 12 MVC No.4324/2022 sitting on the side of the road in front of his house, accident was witnessed by the father of the injured and another person and they took the injured to the hospital, next day police came to the hospital but no FIR was recorded as father of injured was under mental agony and stress and he was more concerned to get the medical treatment to his son.
In that case, complaint was lodged after 3 months of the accident.
Considering the facts and situations of that case, their Lordships held that delay in lodging complaint cannot be a main ground for rejecting the application.
From going through the averments in the complaint and the facts in the present case on hand that immediately after the accident, injured was shifted to Gross Life Hospital.
As deposed by the PW.1 that, as he admitted his daughter at the hospital, 2 days delay has been caused.
Considering the same, delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint is not a ground to reject the petition.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a SCCH - 09 13 MVC No.4324/2022 petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of rider of the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-54-K-6198 which belongs to the Vinutha R vs Manzoor Ilahi on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58048457/
5
respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. ISSUE NO.2:
As per wound certificate - Ex.P.10 discloses that, injury No.1 and 2 are grievous in nature and injury No.3 is simple in nature.
The petitioner got examined Dr.S.A.Somashekara as PW-2 and has produced case sheet at Ex,P.27 and 2 X-rays at Ex.P.28.
PW.2 has deposed that, he has examined petitioner clinically and radiologically as to the assessment of disabilities.

She has met with RTA on 14.07.2022, she was treated at Grass Life SCCH - 09 14 MVC No.4324/2022 hospital,
Bengaluru initially treated at K.K.Hospital.

Bengaluru

sentences.text:
She has diagnosed to have right leg both bones fracture,
she underwent surgery in the Form of CRIF with Tens Nailing on 15.07.2022.
Now on presentation she complains pain and difficulty in running and playing.
On examination she runs with limping wasting of right lower limb is seen surgical scars are seen.
Recent X-ray shows united fractures of both bones right leg.
PW.2 assessed total disability of right limbs at 18% and to whole body at 9%.
Petitioner is said to be a student and the said disabilities in the way of her future career.
14. During cross examination, he has deposed that he has not treated the petitioner personally.
He had denied that present condition of the petitioner is normal and the petitioner can do her work with some difficulty.
He had admitted that, at the time of discharge petitioner condition was stable and there was improvement from discharge to assessing the disability.

PW.2 further admitted that,
there is no difficulty to go to school, further contended that, SCCH - 09 15 MVC No.4324/2022 there is difficulty in future carrier.
He had admitted that, now petitioner is not taking any treatment.
He had denied that, he has assessed higher side disability.
He had deposed that, implants are removed.
He had denied that if implants are removed, no disability will have come.
Further he had admitted that, petitioner came to assess disability after one year eight months.
PW.2 assessed 18% total disability of right limbs and 9% to the whole body.

15. By considering the medical record and opinion of the doctor and also considering the age of the petitioner, who is minor, aged about 9 years at the time of accident, I am of the opinion that, the disability assessed by the doctor is to be taken into consideration i.e., 7% to the whole body as against 9%.
16.
The petitioner was non earning minor girl at the time of accident and was aged about 9 years and student.
She has suffered permanent disablement to the extent of 8%.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 (Mallikarjuna Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another), wherein it was held that - " B. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988-S.166-Just and fair compensation-children suffering disability- Generally-Held, having regard to relevant factors, precedents and approach of various High Courts, appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to actual expenditure for treatment, attendant etc. should be, if disability is above 10% and upto 30% to whole body, Rs.3 lakhs; up to 60%, Rs.4 lakhs; upto Vinutha R vs Manzoor Ilahi on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58048457/
6 90%, Rs.5 lakhs and above 90%, it should be Rs.6 lakhs-For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs.1 lakh, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick".
18.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, the percentage of disability of the petitioner is taken as 7%.
Therefore, it is a fit case to award a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner under the head permanent disability.

19. PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after the accident her daughter took treatment at Grass Life SCCH - 09 17 MVC No.4324/2022 Hospital and as per Ex.P.18 - discharge summary of that hospital,
petitioner took treatment from 28.07.2023 to 29.07.2023 i.e., for 2 days.

entities.text: Grass Life SCCH - 09 17 MVC No.4324/2022 Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the period of treatment, petitioner also required healthy food and extra nourishment.

Considering the said fact,
the Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,000/- under the head Food extra nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.
20. The age of the petitioner was 9 years at the time of accident.
The evidence shows that she has suffered the permanent disability to the extent of 7%.
With this disability she will have to lead her entire life.
So, therefore I deem it proper to award Rs.20,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

21. As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has got marked the bill as per Ex.P.14 i.e.,
27 medical bills.
The total medical bills is of Rs.1,10,683/- as per calculation memo.
The petitioner has also produced 13 medical prescriptions marked at Ex.P.15.
The petitioner SCCH - 09 18 MVC No.4324/2022 has also produced medical bill as per Ex.P.20, it is amount of Rs.65,293/-.
The respondent except mere denial during the cross examination of PW-1 nothing is elicited to refuse the medical expenses under the Ex.P.14 and Ex.P20.
In view of above bills and also nature and gravity of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by her due to such injuries.
The petitioner is entitled for the medical bills under Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.20.

Hence, I proceed to award Rs.1,75,976/- under the head of Medical expenses.
22.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

LIABILITY: On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of objection statement
, it reveals that, the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA- 54-K-6198.

In this case, the respondent No.2 has disputed the negligence on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle as the alleged accident occurred only due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner who was moving on the road negligently and dashed against unknown vehicle and given false complaint against the rider of the vehicle which belongs to respondent No.1.

But during cross examination respondent has not suggested regarding its contention and also he has not produced oral or documentary evidence to prove his defense and it has SCCH - 09 20 MVC No.4324/2022 failed to prove it.
Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the alleged motor cycle and the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of alleged motor cycle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.2,80,976/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
24. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,80,976/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of the policy, the respondent No.2/insurance SCCH - 09 21 MVC No.4324/2022 company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, looking to the medical bill of the petitioner, 75% shall be released in favour of the petitioner through her guardian on proper identification through e-payment and 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner till she attain s the majority,
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
